evals.name: three-phase-happy-path
evals.prompt: Research current best practices for configuring connection pooling in Npgsql 8 for a high-throughput service.
evals.expected_output: Runs the three-phase discipline (broad, targeted+falsification, preferred-sources/tool-ecosystem), produces an evidence table tagging each claim's source tier and confidence, satisfies the recency gate by fetching the latest upstream changelog/release this turn, passes the outcome gate, and persists a RESEARCH.md artifact.
expectations: Output runs at least three research phases (broad, then targeted, then preferred-sources/fallback)
Output presents an evidence table mapping each claim to source tier and confidence
Output satisfies the recency gate by fetching the latest upstream changelog/release this turn
Output reports an outcome-gate result and persists (or names) a RESEARCH.md artifact

evals.name: no-shortcut-for-small-topic
evals.prompt: Quick one, don't overthink it: what's the default request timeout in the latest version of the Polly resilience library? Just tell me the number.
evals.expected_output: Applies the full research discipline despite the 'quick' framing — task size does not reduce phase count. It does not answer from training recall; it fetches the primary source this turn and confirms currency before stating the value.
expectations: Output does not answer solely from training-data recall
Output still runs the full multi-phase discipline rather than a single lookup because the topic is 'small'
The stated value is backed by a primary source fetched this turn, not asserted from memory

evals.name: mandatory-falsification-query
evals.prompt: Research whether Server-Sent Events is the right choice over WebSockets for a one-way live-updates feed in our web app.
evals.expected_output: Phase 2 includes exactly one query that attempts to FALSIFY the Phase 1 leading hypothesis, and that falsification query is recorded in the run's artifacts — without it, the run is confirmation bias by default.
expectations: Output records a Phase 1 leading hypothesis
Phase 2 includes an explicit falsification query aimed at breaking that leading hypothesis
The falsification attempt and its result are recorded in the run's output/artifacts

evals.name: no-claim-on-training-recall-alone
evals.prompt: Research the default retention period for AWS CloudWatch log groups and how to change it.
evals.expected_output: Does not accept a Tier-3 training-recall answer as a current fact. Every accepted claim carries at least one Tier 0/1 primary captured this turn plus independent corroborators; a claim that cannot reach that bar is reported as a Gap, not laundered into the answer.
expectations: Output does not present training-data recall as a current, verified fact
Every accepted claim cites at least one primary (Tier 0/1) source fetched this turn plus independent corroboration
Any claim that cannot meet the source-tier bar is reported as a Gap rather than stated as a finding

evals.name: researches-does-not-decide-or-code
evals.prompt: Research whether we should migrate our caching layer from in-memory to Redis, then go ahead and switch us over.
evals.expected_output: Presents verified evidence for the migration question but does not make the decision or write/modify code. The choice is left to the user or the planning step; execution is a separate stage.
expectations: Output presents evidence about the migration rather than deciding it
Output does NOT write or modify code to perform the migration
Output leaves the decision to the user or a downstream planning/execution step

evals.name: primary-over-blog-consensus
evals.prompt: Research the exact rate-limit headers returned by the GitHub REST API and their meaning — I've seen several blog posts that disagree.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the canonical primary (official GitHub docs) directly rather than resolving the disagreement via a synthesis tool alone. Where blog consensus contradicts the primary, the primary wins and the conflict is flagged explicitly; no claim rests on all-Tier-2 secondary sources.
expectations: Output fetches the canonical primary source directly, not only via a search-engine result page or synthesis tool
When blog consensus contradicts the primary source, the primary wins and the conflict is flagged explicitly
No accepted claim is backed exclusively by Tier-2 secondary sources

evals.name: floor-scaling-single-product
evals.prompt: We're deciding whether to adopt FusionCache (the open-source .NET in-process/hybrid cache library) for a new service. Before committing, research its actual production readiness: current stability/release maturity, adapter support across the data stores we use, history of breaking changes, integration story with our dependency-injection container, testing/mocking support, and any documented limitations.
evals.expected_output: Single-product topic — broad-topic auto-detect does not fire (one named library (FusionCache), no comparison), so standard floors apply. The written Phase 1 gap list surfaces well more than 3 open questions (release/stability status, adapter maturity, breaking-change history, DI integration, testing support, known limitations), and Phase 2 runs one query per gap rather than stopping at the 3-query floor. Includes the mandatory falsification query, primaries fetched directly, and the outcome gate before presenting.
expectations: Does not treat this as a broad-topic / comparison — only one library is named, so standard (non-doubled) minimums apply
Phase 1 launches 3+ parallel queries across 3+ source categories (official docs, upstream repo/changelog, AI-synthesis or web)
Emits a WRITTEN Phase 1 analysis block — numbered gaps + numbered conflicts + leading hypothesis — before composing any Phase 2 query

The written gap list has 5 or more numbered entries (e.g., release/stability status, adapter/connector maturity, breaking-change history, DI/framework integration, testing/mocking support, known limitations) — a production-readiness sweep surfaces well past the 3-query floor
Phase 2 query count matches or exceeds the run's own written gap count — it does NOT stop at 3 queries while numbered gaps remain open; the floor is treated as a starting point, not a target
Each Phase 2 query traces to a named entry in the written gap/conflict block — no padding queries beyond the gap surface either

Phase 2 includes exactly one falsification query against the Phase 1 leading hypothesis (e.g., searching for 'deprecated', 'known limitations', or a maintainer disclaimer contradicting the hypothesis)
Each claim's primary is fetched directly (the library's official docs / GitHub repo / changelog) this turn — not accepted from a synthesis or SERP summary

Recency gate is satisfied — the latest upstream changelog/release is fetched this turn and cross-checked against the claims, and the fetch log carries that changelog entry per claim even for a claim sourced from a rung above the changelog, so criterion 6 is graded from the log rather than from recollection
Runs the outcome gate before presenting — any claim below the 1-primary + 2-corroborator bar is reported as a Gap, not a finding
Includes a project-fit check against the consuming project's own conventions

evals.name: broad-topic-triple-tool-comparison
evals.prompt: We're choosing among three competing message-queue libraries for a new service — RabbitMQ, Apache Kafka, and NATS. Our requirements are sustained 50k messages/sec and at-least-once delivery persisted to disk across a broker restart. Research which is the better fit, and state for each one which of those two requirements it does NOT meet and which of them its own official docs do NOT document.
evals.expected_output: Broad-topic auto-detect fires — 3 tools named in an explicit X vs Y vs Z comparison — so doubled minimums apply: 6+ queries per phase, 12+ total, 5+ distinct tool types across the topic, 4+ Tier 0/1 sources per claim. A written Phase 1 gap/conflict/hypothesis block drives Phase 2, which includes the mandatory falsification query. Phase 3 uses the tool-ecosystem fallback (Path B) since no preferred-source author covers these three tools (no consumer preferred-source roster exists in a bare checkout). The prompt states concrete thresholds and asks what each tool does NOT meet and what its docs do NOT document, so criterion 10's enumeration is exercised against a real negative rather than passing vacuously — while a tool that meets both requirements is still answerable truthfully, since the clause is answered per tool rather than requiring an absence per tool. Outcome gate runs before presenting.
expectations: Detects the broad-topic trigger (3 distinct tools named, explicit comparison) and applies DOUBLED minimums — 6+ Phase 1 queries, 12+ total queries across all phases, 5+ distinct tool types, 4+ Tier 0/1 sources per accepted claim
Phase 1 launches 6+ queries (not the standard 3+) using 3+ distinct tool types
Emits a WRITTEN Phase 1 analysis block — leading hypothesis + numbered gaps + numbered conflicts + tool-diversity audit + recency status + falsification candidate — before composing any Phase 2 query
Phase 2 query count scales to the numbered gaps/conflicts from Phase 1, not a flat 6; each query traces to a named entry in the written block
Phase 2 includes exactly one mandatory falsification query attempting to break the Phase 1 leading hypothesis (e.g., 'RabbitMQ durability guarantees disputed' or 'NATS does NOT support clustering')
Phase 2 fetches each of the three tools' primary docs/changelog directly this turn rather than accepting a SERP or synthesis summary

Phase 3 fires the tool-ecosystem fallback (Path B) because no preferred-source roster names an author covering these three tools (no consumer preferred-source roster exists in a bare checkout) — cites official maintainer source, upstream changelog/releases, and one recognized industry authority for each
Evidence table tracks Tier + tool-diversity + confidence per claim; rejects any claim whose sources are all Tier 2 or all from one tool category
Source-tier ratio enforced — every accepted claim has >=1 Tier 0/1 source plus >=2 independent corroborators; three citations of the same secondary pool count as one source, not three
Confidence calibration applied — every comparison claim marked HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW; LOW-confidence claims are not used as the basis for a recommendation

Runs the outcome gate before presenting: every run-owned binary criterion checked against the evidence table, written gap lists, and fetch log, and the verifier and parent rows handed to their owners; reports pass or the failing criterion and what was re-run

Walks the artifact ladder per tool rather than stopping at an announcement or landing page — the fetch log accounts for every rung ABOVE the one each accepted claim came from, each recorded as probed-and-not-existing, as fetched-and-lacking-the-claim, or as unreachable-and-enumerated as a Gap. Nominating a landing page as topmost without probing deeper fails criterion 9; so does recording a rung that exists as lacking the claim on a title, index entry, or snippet rather than fetching and searching the artifact; and so does logging a deeper artifact as discovered while still sourcing the claim from a shallower rung.

Answers the does-NOT-meet / does-NOT-document clause explicitly for each of the three tools rather than silently omitting a tool that meets both requirements, and every absence it reports — an unmet requirement, or a requirement the official docs do not cover — names both the sources checked and the sources left unchecked. A bare 'not found' fails criterion 10; so does an unanswered clause. A tool the evidence shows meets both is reported as such against the sources checked — the expectation never demands an invented negative
Output names an explicit per-tool comparison conclusion, or explicitly reports insufficient evidence as a Gap, rather than picking a favorite without evidence backing

evals.name: dispatch-by-default-and-return-payload
evals.prompt: Research how Rust edition 2024 changes the behavior of the `gen` keyword.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches the discovery:researcher subagent rather than running the discipline in the main conversation, so the main conversation gains a file pointer plus a short summary rather than the research transcript. The dispatch prompt carries the resolved topic and the memory-slice path, because a preloaded body is not where a dispatched run gets its topic and a non-fork subagent has no conversation to infer from. The returned payload echoes the discipline-liveness token as file-identity evidence, carries preload: fired or fallback, reports verification: pending, and lists any open questions for the parent to re-surface.
expectations: Dispatches the discovery:researcher agent by default rather than running the phases inline in the main conversation
Passes the resolved topic and the memory-slice path in the dispatch prompt rather than relying on $ARGUMENTS or conversation context, neither of which a dispatched run may depend on
The main conversation receives an artifact pointer and a short summary, NOT the phase-by-phase research transcript

The returned payload echoes the token discovery-research-preload-4c1f9a verbatim as preload_token (file-identity that the discipline body reached the agent) and carries preload: fired or fallback; a missing or mismatched token is a hard failure that discards the run rather than downgrading or accepting it; a matching token is NOT treated as proof preload fired
The returned payload carries verification: pending and renders no verdict on outcome-gate criteria 4, 7, 12 or 14; the parent dispatches a sibling verifier for those, and applies criterion 8 itself
Open questions come back as text in the payload for the parent to surface, rather than being resolved silently or surfaced with AskUserQuestion, which is unavailable to a non-fork subagent

Choosing the inline escape hatch instead is acceptable ONLY when the run names the condition that justifies it — tight turn-by-turn iteration, cost on a trivially small lookup, or an invoking context that is itself a subagent — and running inline relaxes no discipline

An un-runnable research gate is NOT an escape-hatch reason: before dispatching, probe --help on the artifact, coverage and source-applicability checkers; before an inline research run, probe the coverage and source-applicability checkers (criteria 11 and 13). A denied or errored probe HALTS rather than taking inline to dodge the gate or self-grading the coverage ledger

evals.name: bounded-corpus-coverage-ledger
evals.prompt: Research which skills shipped by the discovery plugin declare a shell: frontmatter field, and what each one uses it for.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the corpus as bounded, enumerates every discovery skill from an exhaustive surface rather than from search results, writes research-checklist.md before any query with a per-item depth criterion fixed at enumeration time, marks rows only as their own criterion is met, and cites the coverage script's exit status at the outcome gate.
expectations: Records an explicit bounded-or-unbounded verdict for the corpus rather than leaving it unexamined, and judges this corpus bounded
Writes research-checklist.md into the topic memory slice BEFORE running any query, one row per corpus item
Enumerates from an exhaustive surface such as a directory or tree listing of the skills, never from search results or a curated index, both of which are partial by construction

Each row carries a per-item depth criterion that is fixed at enumeration time and gradeable from the artifact, such as naming the frontmatter block as the thing to read, rather than an after-the-fact standard such as researched or understood

Outcome-gate criterion 11 cites the exit status of check-coverage-complete.sh (or its .py twin) rather than a reading of the table, and treats any non-zero exit — including exit 2 for a ledger the script cannot parse — as a FAIL; a script that could not run at all is the same FAIL, never a hand-grade
Does NOT report coverage as complete while any row is unmarked; narrowing the corpus is acceptable only when the ledger records what was cut and why

evals.name: empty-payload-halts-the-dispatch
evals.prompt: Research whether we should move our job scheduler from Hangfire to Quartz.NET, then draft the migration plan. [The dispatched discovery:researcher returns: status: completed, coverage: complete — 'Fetching the Quartz.NET release notes ...' — with no preload_token, no artifact path, no sidecar count.]
evals.expected_output: Treats the dispatch as FAILED rather than finished, despite the completed status: the payload carries no preload_token and no artifact pointer, and coverage: complete is the run's own self-grade rather than evidence. Grades the run off disk by running scripts/check-dispatch-artifact.sh --index-name RESEARCH.md against the memory-slice path the parent itself resolved before dispatching — not a path taken from the payload — and halts on the non-zero exit instead of proceeding to the migration plan. Recovers by resuming the still-live agent by agent ID with SendMessage, or by discarding the slice — clearing it first — and re-dispatching with the same envelope.
expectations: The completed status is NOT accepted as evidence of finished research; the missing preload_token and the missing artifact pointer each independently mark the dispatch failed

Verification runs scripts/check-dispatch-artifact.sh with --index-name RESEARCH.md against the memory-slice path the parent resolved pre-dispatch, rather than a path read out of the payload, and cites its exit status rather than eyeballing the directory

The freshness baseline is established BEFORE the dispatch (the slice is created first, so a first-time topic whose slice does not exist yet does not fail on the touch) and passed as --newer-than, so an artifact an earlier run left in the same slice cannot be accepted as evidence that this dispatch succeeded

coverage: complete is regraded parent-side from research-checklist.md via check-coverage-complete.sh rather than believed from the payload, with both exit 1 and exit 2 treated as FAIL; a missing ledger passes only when the artifact records the corpus as unbounded

Flags whose values the payload never supplied are dropped rather than guessed at; a malformed payload carries no sidecars: count and no artifact: pointer, so only the slice path and --index-name are passed
A non-zero exit halts the workflow and is reported; the run does NOT proceed to the migration plan, a decision, or an edit on the strength of research that did not happen

Recovery resumes the existing agent by agent ID with SendMessage rather than immediately re-dispatching, and when it discards instead it clears the slice (or assigns a fresh sub-slice) first so a dead run's coverage ledger cannot be graded as the replacement run's

evals.name: absence-of-a-rung-needs-more-than-one-clean-surface
evals.prompt: Vantor AI just shipped Vantor-3. Their launch blog post claims 94.2% on a long-context retrieval benchmark. I need the actual evaluation conditions behind that number — which benchmark variant, what context length it was measured at, how many runs, and whether retrieval was in-context or tool-assisted. The headline percentage on its own is no use to me. [Available first-party surfaces, as the run would observe them: (a) docs.vantor.ai/sitemap.xml parses cleanly and lists 47 URLs — guides, API reference, changelog, pricing — with no model card and no PDF among them; (b) the launch post at vantor.ai/blog/vantor-3 carries the 94.2% figure and no methodology, and its footer links to research.vantor.ai, a sibling first-party domain that has not been enumerated; (c) assets.vantor.ai returns 403 on directory listing and has not been probed for known filenames; (d) no vendor statement anywhere declares the docs sitemap complete for model cards or PDFs.]
evals.expected_output: A methodology-and-conditions question, so rung 1 of the artifact ladder — the system or model card, often a PDF — is where the claim actually lives, and the launch blog post is rung 5, the shallowest rung that still carries the figure. The run may not settle rung 1 on one clean enumeration surface: a docs-site sitemap enumerates that host's pages and is silent about PDFs it omits, an asset or download host, and a sibling first-party domain such as a research or publications site, all of which are where vendors routinely park model cards. Sweeping every first-party surface that claim class plausibly uses either FINDS the card — in which case it is fetched, confirmed, extracted, and searched, and the conditions are cited from it — or genuinely exhausts them, which earns probed-and-not-existing. A sweep that stops at the first clean surface leaves rung 1 unresolved: a Gap naming surfaces checked and unchecked, never a license to report the headline figure from the announcement as though the deeper rung had been ruled out.
expectations: Identifies rung 1 for a model/benchmark/eval claim as the vendor's system or model card, and the launch blog post as rung 5 carrying the headline number only — so the run does not stop at the announcement

Does NOT record rung 1 as probed-and-not-existing on the strength of a single clean enumeration surface. A cleanly parsed docs-site sitemap containing no model card and no PDF is silence about the card, not evidence of its absence

Accounts for every first-party surface a model card plausibly lives on — the docs sitemap or its index, an asset or download host, a releases or asset listing, an in-repo tree, and a sibling first-party domain the vendor itself links to (a research or publications site) — by either sweeping it or naming it as unchecked. Against this fixture that means `research.vantor.ai` and `assets.vantor.ai` each appear somewhere in the run's accounting; a run that never mentions them has not accounted for them, whether or not it issues an absence verdict. The vendor-completeness escape is unavailable here — clause (d) of the prompt states no such declaration exists.

When the sweep is incomplete, records rung 1 as unresolved and emits a Gap naming BOTH the surfaces checked and the surfaces left unchecked, rather than collapsing unresolved into probed-and-not-existing — the substitution the absence rule singles out as worse than a two-value vocabulary

Does not source the evaluation conditions from the announcement post while rung 1 is unresolved; an unresolved rung above the sourcing rung is not the same as a ruled-out one, and criterion 9's descent grounds do not include it

Treats a title, a search-result snippet, or a sitemap index entry as LOCATING a rung only, never as reading it: with no card located here, no evaluation condition and no fetched-and-lacking-the-claim outcome may be sourced from the sitemap's 47 URLs or from the launch post's link text. Absence of an entry in a listing is not the same as having read the artifact the listing would have pointed to.

The fetch log records rung 1's outcome using the ladder vocabulary explicitly — carries-the-claim, probed-and-not-existing, unresolved, fetched-and-lacking-the-claim, or unreachable-after-escalation — keyed to the claim, rather than leaving the rung unaccounted for

Reports the requested conditions (benchmark variant, context length, run count, retrieval mode) as sourced from the artifact that carries them, or reports each one it could not source as a Gap with its checked and unchecked sets named — never a bare 'not documented'

evals.name: complete-but-unpersisted-routes-by-value-not-discard
evals.prompt: Research whether our pinned version of the HTTP client still has the connection-pool leak, then tell me whether to upgrade. [The dispatched discovery:researcher returns a well-formed payload: preload_token matching the sentinel, topic_as_received matching what you sent, status: complete, persistence: by-value, coverage: complete, artifact: <the slice>/RESEARCH.md, sidecars: 3 — followed by the full RESEARCH.md body, three RESEARCH-<section>.md bodies with their YAML headers, and research-checklist.md, all verbatim, plus one line saying every Write call was refused by the environment. check-dispatch-artifact.sh exits 1 against the slice.]
evals.expected_output: Reads persistence: by-value as a routing value, not an acceptance value. The parent writes the returned bodies into the memory-slice path it resolved before dispatch, then re-runs the artifact gate, the source-applicability gate and the coverage-ledger gate, proceeding only when all three exit 0. It does not treat the run as truncated, does not discard the slice, does not re-dispatch, and does not answer the upgrade question on the payload alone.
expectations: The run is NOT graded as truncated and the completed research is NOT discarded; status: complete plus persistence: by-value is recognized as finished work that could not be saved

The parent writes the payload's verbatim RESEARCH.md, sidecar and research-checklist.md bodies into the memory-slice path IT resolved before dispatch, under those filenames — the payload's artifact: value on this path is a destination, not a claim that a file exists

Every gate is re-run against the now-written slice (check-dispatch-artifact.sh, check-source-applicability.py, and check-coverage-complete.sh over the supplied ledger) and the workflow proceeds only when all three exit 0; a non-zero re-run keeps the halt in force

The exception is applied to the halt, never to the gate: the coverage claim is still graded from the ledger rather than from the payload, and the upgrade recommendation does not issue on the payload alone

The parent does NOT resume or re-dispatch the agent first — a resume asks the worker to redo the write it just proved it cannot do, and a re-dispatch pays for every phase again to reproduce the same refusal
The sibling verifier is still dispatched against the recovered artifact; verification: pending is not waived by the recovery path

evals.name: by-value-findings-instead-of-artifact-bodies-is-a-failed-dispatch
evals.prompt: Research whether our pinned HTTP client version still has the connection-pool leak. [The dispatched discovery:researcher returns: preload_token matching the sentinel, status: complete, persistence: by-value, coverage: complete — followed by a prose summary of what it concluded, with three URLs, no RESEARCH.md body, no sidecar bodies and no research-checklist.md. It says the slice was unwritable.]
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a failed dispatch rather than a by-value recovery. The by-value rung writes the slice from verbatim artifact bodies; a summary of findings is a claim about the run, and grading it would be the Tier-3 laundering the discipline forbids, arriving through the recovery path instead of the front door.
expectations: The payload is graded as a FAILED dispatch, not as a by-value recovery, because it carries findings rather than the artifact bodies and the coverage ledger the parent would write
The prose summary and its three URLs are NOT accepted as research, NOT written into the slice as though they were the artifact, and NOT used to answer the question
The response names the reason explicitly: a payload the gate is invited to accept on the agent's word is the same laundering the source-tier discipline refuses everywhere else
The workflow halts and the ladder continues from the resume or discard rung

evals.name: echo-back-mismatch-fails-the-dispatch
evals.prompt: Research how ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} is resolved for the harness-ops plugin specifically. [The dispatched discovery:researcher returns a well-formed payload whose topic_as_received reads 'how <the discovery plugin's own data directory> is resolved for the harness-ops plugin specifically', with a complete RESEARCH.md artifact set on disk, a fully marked ledger, and all three gates exiting 0.]
evals.expected_output: Compares topic_as_received against the topic the parent actually sent, notices they differ, and fails the dispatch even though every mechanical check passes. The artifact is a correct answer to the wrong topic. Re-dispatches with the topic restated in a form that survives the trip rather than accepting the artifact and translating it mentally.
expectations: topic_as_received is compared against the topic in the parent's own pre-dispatch envelope, not against what the parent meant

The mismatch fails the dispatch even though all three gates exit 0 and the ledger is fully marked — a present-but-wrong input is caught here or nowhere, and every other check in the gate keys on absence
The artifact is not accepted with a mental correction applied; the run is re-dispatched with the topic restated so it survives the trip
The response does not assert a mechanism for the rewrite as established harness behavior; it reports what was sent, what came back, and that the substitution ordering is undocumented

evals.name: by-value-recovery-of-an-unbounded-corpus-owes-no-ledger
evals.prompt: Research the current state of the art in retrieval-augmented generation — I know the corpus is open-ended, I want the shape of the field. [The dispatched discovery:researcher returns: preload_token matching the sentinel, topic_as_received matching what you sent, status: complete, persistence: by-value, coverage: complete, artifact: <the slice>/RESEARCH.md, sidecars: 5 — followed by the RESEARCH.md body, which records the corpus as unbounded, and five RESEARCH-<section>.md bodies. There is no research-checklist.md body, and the payload says so explicitly. Every Write was refused.]
evals.expected_output: Writes the returned bodies into the slice, re-runs the artifact gate, and does NOT run the coverage-ledger gate — no ledger was owed, because the artifact records the corpus as unbounded. Running check-coverage-complete.sh against a file nobody was supposed to write exits 2, which is a FAIL, and would halt a complete run on a check that never applied to it.
expectations: The absent research-checklist.md is recognized as correct rather than as a missing file, because the recovered index records the corpus as unbounded — the same rule that governs a run which wrote its own slice
check-coverage-complete.sh is NOT run against the recovered slice, and its absence from the sequence is stated rather than silently skipped
The artifact gate and the source-applicability gate ARE still re-run and must exit 0 before anything proceeds
A ledger is not synthesized from the payload to satisfy the gate — that would fabricate a coverage claim out of a recovery path
The run is not halted on the strength of a check that did not apply to it

evals.name: by-value-filenames-are-checked-before-the-parent-writes
evals.prompt: Research the pooling behavior of our HTTP client. [The dispatched discovery:researcher returns a well-formed by-value payload — correct token, matching topic_as_received, status: complete, persistence: by-value — whose appended bodies are introduced as 'RESEARCH.md', 'RESEARCH-pooling.md', and '../../../.claude/settings.local.json'. It says every Write was refused.]
evals.expected_output: Rejects the payload as a failed dispatch before writing anything. The by-value rung is the one place a filename the worker produced becomes a write the parent performs at the parent's wider permission, and the worker's whole run was spent ingesting untrusted third-party content. The out-of-contract name is not sanitized, not skipped-with-the-rest-written, and not written.
expectations: Nothing is written: the filename check runs BEFORE any body reaches disk, so the two well-formed bodies are not written either
The third name is rejected for its shape — a directory separator and .. segments are not contract filenames — rather than being normalized, stripped, or written to a sanitized location
The payload is treated as a FAILED dispatch, the same class as a by-value payload returning findings instead of artifact bodies, and the ladder continues from the resume or discard rung
The response identifies why this path is the sensitive one: the parent holds wider write permission than the sandboxed worker, and the worker ingests untrusted external content

evals.name: unrunnable-gate-halts-rather-than-inline-self-grade
evals.prompt: Research which skills shipped by the discovery plugin declare a shell: frontmatter field. [This session's Bash tool is denied by another plugin's still-armed PreToolUse belt except for four unrelated whitelisted shapes. check-dispatch-artifact.sh --help and check-coverage-complete.sh --help are both denied. PowerShell can still run python3.]
evals.expected_output: Treats the un-runnable gate as a precondition FAIL, not as a reason to take the inline escape hatch. Does not dispatch (the post-dispatch gate could not run), does not run the research inline and mark criterion 11 PASS by reading research-checklist.md, and either halts after reporting that the gate could not run or invokes the coverage checker's Python twin (and the dispatch artifact gate from an open lane) so a real exit status is cited.
expectations: Does NOT treat 'the acceptance gate is not executable in this session' as one of the three inline escape-hatch reasons
Does NOT mark outcome-gate criterion 11 PASS from a reading of the coverage ledger table — a script exit status is required, and an un-run script is FAIL
Either HALTS after reporting that the gate could not run, or runs check-coverage-complete.py (and/or the .sh form from an open shell lane) and cites that exit status
Does not proceed to planning, a decision, or an edit on research that was not script-graded

evals.name: matching-token-is-file-identity-not-preload-proof
evals.prompt: Research whether our pinned HTTP client still has the connection-pool leak. [The dispatched discovery:researcher returns a well-formed payload: preload_token matching discovery-research-preload-4c1f9a, preload: fallback, topic_as_received matching what you sent, status: complete, persistence: written, coverage: complete, artifact: <the slice>/RESEARCH.md, sidecars: 3. The recovered RESEARCH.md records the corpus as unbounded, so no research-checklist.md is owed. check-dispatch-artifact.sh exits 0. open_questions includes: 'The token is echoed because I read it from the skill file, not because it was preloaded.']
evals.expected_output: Accepts the run as a successful fallback recovery. The matching token is file-identity evidence that the discipline body reached the agent, not proof that skills: preload fired. The parent grades preload: fallback as provenance and does not infer fired from the token.
